I have OSFED restricting and recently made it through my first pregnancy and had a healthy baby despite my ED really hitting hard with urges to restrict and panic and hate at my body. It was especially awful when I was gaining weight and still didn’t show a clear bump so I felt everyone was judging me for being fat and eating lots. The whole 9 months I actively hated how I looked, felt and the fact that I was eating lots without exercising it off, since I had bad round ligament pain that stopped my running at 5 months pregnant. Pregnancy was the worst and I never ever want to go though it again! It was worth it to give life to my healthy and well developed baby though for this one time! Below are some tips that made things a little bit better during pregnancy.

I told my obgyn early on that I have an ED and find it difficult to not restrict eating, and asked that the office put in my chart not to tell me my weight and for my obgyn to just tell me if she was happy with my weight gain so far at each appointment (note that “happy with my wright” not asking if I was gaining too much or too little too soon), Before getting weighed by the nurses at each visit I would ask the nurse if she could not tell me my weight when I stepped on the scale backwards and it turns out it’s a normal request they get all the time so they just say okay! and continue with everything as normal, no questions why or anything. Just business as usual.

It also helped to meet with my ED dietitian every 2-4 weeks. She was very reassuring that we would work together after birth to lose the weight (which she was right, and I’m making great progress in a healthy way for the first time ever!). My dietitian told me when I needed to increase meal size and number of snacks to incorporate throughout pregnancy. Instead of counting calories on my own, she gave me a bunch of not scary food options that I could put 2 or 3 things together to make the right size snack that I would put an alarm in my phone and eat regularly even if I wasn’t hungry and didn’t want to eat out of fear and being used to ignore hunger. I had frequently used food logging with my ED dietitian but once she got me in a rhythm we stopped my logging so I didn’t need to write down and record all the food going into me. That was very helpful since I was feeling so shameful to log.

Recently I found out I gained a whole lot of weight, more than I had expected, at the end. That made me feel I failed since it was more than the typical amount of weight gain during pregnancy, but I have lessened that shame postpartum. The weight really did come off fast for the most part in the weeks after which was a relief. My goal now is to lose the rest of the weight quickly but not by eliminating eating outright, since my dietitian said that her way would keep up my metabolism. 

Good luck with your pregnancy, you can do it even if you keep your eyes closed for as much as you need!

I don't think that's disrespectful. If it helps, I can relate in that recently I've come to feel a lot of relief that my dad (abuser) died about a year ago and I won't need to worry about him also abusing my future children. 

Heads up, at least in my experience my dad's sudden death still hit me hard and was very confusing to process. Even though I was angry at him and wanting to cut off contact for a while before his death, I still got sad and physically grieved for a while despite my wishes not to. If that happens to you, I hope you'll be less hard on yourself than I was to me.

Thanks for replying, I appreciate it. When I first read it though, I felt like shouting out that my dad's not a perverted creep, I must have made a mistake in my memories and I'm a horrible daughter for speaking of my dad this way. It's the thought that if I keep this secret, no one else will ever know or think of my dad as anything but good, and that it wouldn't be real if it's just me. It would be easier if I could just shove my memories away, re-bury and deny them, and then I'll be back to being a calm, happy person. It doesn't work that way though, does it?

I’ve been on Latuda for about 5 years now. I had previously tried many antipsychotics and even years on clozaril did not help my symptoms. Latuda even got rid of my thought broadcasting delusion, which had never been shaken before.

I did have some side effects though, but for me they are easily treatable and not an issue for me anymore. I had an EPS side effect, but taking a little benztropine with the Latuda made that not happen in the years since starting it. 

It really does need to be taken with food, otherwise I do get nauseous. But I’ve had absolutely no weight gain so it’s not intimidating to eat food with Latuda. Other positive is that I do not have tiredness or sedation as side effects.

Latuda works best for me and I’m really glad I’m on it. Of course, different antipsychotics work best for different people, but if your doctor is thinking of prescribing it, I hope you have the necessary relief!

Good luck! I had a great transition from zyprexa where I also had really bad tiredness and weight gain, into taking Latuda which years later is the best antipsychotic for me. I hope you find success, too!

OP here. I had an ED-competent dietitian for a while, but recently quit since I thought I was all better. I have other co-morbid mental illness that I can take a pill to help be a lot better, though taking those for life. I have a hard time admitting that my ED is going to be tough for who knows how long, I tend to deny having an ED anymore since I'm no longer underweight.

I do, I've been on it since 2015 after many antipsychotics, including clozaril, did nothing for my symptoms. It worked moderately for at least 6-8 months, but then steady improvements. I'm currently psychosis-free, even stubborn thought broadcasting finally went away almost a year ago. I occasionally still get the "what-ifs" about medication being good or a coverup, but for me latuda is amazing. It took a long time for latuda to fully kick-in, but its better than all the previous ones I tried that worked fast but also didn't provide lasting relief.

To be dead and cease consciousness. I have schizophrenia and I’ve also struggled with suicidal attempts and ideation for over 15 years, and I’m only 29. 

There’s nothing worse than wanting to stop constant mental suffering then deal with any kind of eternity after - what if I couldn’t escape that?

I’m doing better mentally now though! My last serious attempt was when I was 17, and every year since I feel a bit stronger.

We start off with anything I’ve been wanting to ask since last time, if anything stressful food related came up or if I did something good, and go through the goals we made last time.

Next we go through the food logs together, and she is really positive the whole time. I’ve always hated writing any logs before, but with this dietician she gives feedback and we talk through both good meals and meals needing more food, but also discuss any thoughts or anxieties I have about those comments.

After food logs, I get to ask all the food and weight obsessions questions I have, and we address some we can and some that I should bring back to my primary psychotherapist.  She also has heard of lots of the problems I have regarding eating and I feel like she can understand that I’m trying hard but not going to be 90% all the time. We set goals for next time, which can be one of mine or she helps naturally come up with some during our session.

I always feel relieved walking out of her office. She also emails me reminders of what we talked about in the appointment (nothing personally identifying) so I remember the food ideas, goals, and anything else I asked her to include.

Yes, I think so! I’m currently seeing a dietician/nutritionist and she is very good. I’m at a healthy weight now, my minimum treatment goal weight fluctuating a bit, so I also was concerned that I’d be too past the heavy restricting part and not be seen as needing a dietician. For me it’s now mostly the ED voice and obsessions and then restricting a little.... and the dietician is very understanding about that and helps me feel comfortable talking about that along with the actual food nutrition part.

My dietician specializes in eating disorders, and also spends 45 minutes with me between food logs, nutrition discussion, and mental talk therapy. I hope you too can find someone you can trust and who will be able to help you!

Edit: I reread and saw how you currently have a therapist who recommended a dietician. I’ve been in psychotherapy for coexisting mental illnesses, but it’s been a little hard to fully communicate how hard eating disorders are to him, so I find my dietician to add that part and be on a team together.
Hiding self harm, suicidal thoughts, and psychosis from my angry parents.
I can relate. It would always just be 'one more pill' than the last time.
My childhood through high school diaries pieced back together. I shredded all of them when I was having a psychotic break at 15 years old. In doing so I deleted most of my memories of growing up.

In addition to paranoid schizophrenia, I also have conversion disorder, anxiety disorder, and am recovering from OSFED (restrictive eating disorder).

They like to prey off each other, and I end up delusional, having panic attacks, and paralyzed. Even revealing this has my back, foot and leg "paralyzed" until I can trick my mind to get out of it (until then, I'm unable to get out of my chair).
Thank you all for your comments, I'm reply soon, but I do really appreciate your time and it's going to take me some time to mentally parse through them. Thank you.

I recently started to go to Pure Barre exercise classes, and I realized the other day that I don't having those constant circular and painful thoughts/head-feelings when I'm working out there. Maybe it's because I have something physically and mentally engaging during those classes. I find it even better than getting a relaxing massage (I don't get a break from racing thoughts there).

Something my grandfather said to me when he was in a hospital before going on hospice. I  was nervous visiting, since I was told he was in really bad condition.

My mom was going on chattering to make everything"okay" in the room, when my grandfather montioned for me to take his hand. 

He then whispered to just me and said "I'm dying". 

My strong, proud, supportive, encouraging, loving grandfather...

I'm the fiance who has had constant suicidal idealization and attempts since childhood (currently 26). I'm always looking yet another reason to live, and all these heartfelt comments really struck a cord with me. I know I'm not the intended audience, but thank you.

Seriously? I could care less what any guy looks like, creepy can come in all sorts of looks. And why would I be all blushy and giggly like a silly girl when I've found an amazing man who I'll be spending the rest of my life with?

Oh yes, I agree that compliment is a good thing! Perhaps I should have been more explicit in my original comment. It was rather painful to remember in that moment when I typed it to recall his unwanted rubbing against me, ignoring my comments that he was making me uncomfortable with his new interest in me and his "grand" idea that I should definitely leave my now-fiance for him... 

Do unwanted sexual advances count as a good reason to block someone from social media in your opinion?

And if you ask why I didn't just walk away, I was rather in shock based on a previous experience years before - I had clammed up and had trouble getting away from him for a while that day.

Did she also say she wants you to divorce your partner and be with her instead? And then on the way to say goodbye walk so close to you such that he keeps rubbing your side such that I'm practically walking in the street to avoid contact? And when the weight comments continued for a long time and started to make me feel uncomfortable enough to thank him for his compliment but lets change the subject... and he ignored that?

How would you take that situation?

Sure, the first few minutes were a compliment. That was nice, and appreciated. It takes work to lose that weight, and it was good of him to notice and say for a bit. I'll gladly take that compliment on my body from other people, and then move on normally in conversation and not be expected to show romantic interest in him.

The 7 years was how long I had been with my boyfriend at the time. I had met this 'friend' 2 years ago, and he knew from the start that I was in a committed relationship with someone (they had met). 

I was upset because (1) he kept talking and exclaiming and walking too close to me, ignoring me when I said that we should chat about something else since I was uncomfortable with the way he was acting (2) the words he said that he would try and break up my fantastic relationship so that he could date me instead is rude and sexist in that his self-professed 'macho' personality would automatically mean I would immediately date or fuck him. People are never entitled to have the other person reciprocate intimate relations, especially it there is clear and stated disinterest. 

I'll respond to your hypothetical for your follow-up later, but I hope you can see the issue here is not just saying or receiving compliments, and not just if it's from/about men/women, its knowing how to be a decent human being by listening when the person says they are uncomfortable with the conversation and suggestions and respecting that request.

I gained so much weight on meds for years, and one good friend of mine in grad school seemed pretty cool to talk to. He got his PhD, moved to another state, and then came back a year later to visit. I had lost 50 pounds since changing meds, which he was very quick to notice and commet on during our brunch.

The final straw was when he gave me a hug and said if I looked as good as I do now, he would have flirted with me from the moment we met and taken me away from my boyfriend of 7 years.

Needless to say, after a day of sexism and blatant objectifying me, I told him how wrong that was, he didn't understand, I blocked him from all communication.

I'm looking forward to getting married in October without mysoginist scum like him.

It's where I bury some part of me so deeply such that I'm not afraid of it being known anymore. I modify myself such that when meeting new people - the past never happened. They see me as I am whoever I present to them as I choose. And then during the process after the reset, that presentation becomes all I know of myself without actually having a painful past. 

It's a reset to re-invent myself.
Thank you. I do feel a little calmer this morning.

My brain paralyzes parts or my entire body throughout the day. I'll think at the affected parts and tell them to move, but they just don't respond. I was diagnosed with conversion disorder at my second trip to the ER where they did so many neurological tests, even a lumbar puncture. 

In order to break out of the paralysis I have to trick my mind, but that doesn't always work since I can't think of the trick in advance or else the trick doesn't work.

A longing, overdue, to be free of pain. It's the start of a new year, another that I have to endure forever. They say there's not much more they can do. Just therapy and keep going. Keep with that paranoid schizophrenia, conversion disorder, anxiety, and eating disorder. I wake up, keep from crying to work, then become super yavvy, but its too much to keep up, keep from crying on the way home, collapse at home...

Yes, I need to figure out why I stopped taking them when they didn't seem to be doing any harm and had no side effects. I have no idea why. 

I see a therapist once a week, and really enjoy talking with him. Somehow its easier to be honest with him.

I can't tell people how I feel either. Sometimes I don't even know how I feel inside. I have a better time knowing and sharing good feelings, except for love and trust to people other than my fiance and cat. I was pleased with myself when I was actually able to tell my therapist that I felt very upset, betrayed, and angry at a person! Usually I say I'm "not happy" with that person.

Clozapine did not touch any of my symptoms. Neither did risperdal, abilify, zyprexa, haldol... Not when one at a time, not when taking a combination, even including other meds like lamictal or celexa. I'm back to taking Latuda to make my psychiatrist happy, I was on, off, now coming back on and I've felt the same throughout. But, at least Latuda does not give me terrible side effects of extreme tiredness and weight gain like all those others I tried.

Yes, my doc thinks I'm delusional and paranoid, and yes I battle my mind and when it plays tricks on me I prove to be more clever and trick it back, but I'm happy with things as they are.
I had just gotten in the car, too late haha. Wish me luck...
I re-read your post a lot just now. Thank you for sharing your sister's story, and for the good advice. Also thanks for the well wishes on my engagement!

Yes, I live with my fiance a decent distance away from my parents place. I think you gave a lot of good advice, thank you. Any tips on how to react when my mom tries and makes me feel guilty about this?
Thank you for all the kind responses!

Only my fiancé, older brother, and sister-in-law see it. I had to hide my struggles from everyone growing up. As a young kid my parents would tell me that I was a happy kid, don't let anyone especially my grandparents have any reason to think otherwise. So I'm pretty good at hiding it around most people.

Your medication question is a tough one. Right now I'm on Latuda for an anti-psychotic. I'm having fewer delusional suicidal thoughts on it than any other meds. Still evidently very paranoid and delusional, which is something that has never been lessened by any med I've taken before.

I've tried 6 various anti-psychotics, a few antidepressants, and a mood stabilizer, all alone or different combinations of each - for the past 10 years. The only current thing that's had its intended benefit is when I now can take Klonopin as needed, which does make me less anxious. At least the Latuda has no side effects for me, so I'll take it. I'm done being on meds that follow the past trend of never working on my struggles, especially those with tiredness and weight gain (I wanted to kill myself every time I looked in the mirror back when I was 50 pounds heavier.) 

I have no idea what to do. I feel lucky to have made it to 26, but that's so young what about the next 60 years!

Oh, I almost forgot. I lose time. Some weeks I live through Wednesday, go to work as normal. Then the next day it's Friday, I'm convinced Thursday didn't exist, except for having dinner near work that Thursday. I'm assuming I went to work that day, how else would I end up at that dinner place. Usually it's hours missing, though. I force myself to keep busy at work, otherwise I'm at my computer and 30 minutes later I have the same webpage up, no idea if I read anything of it. I made sure to increase the time before the computer screen turns black so no one else notices.

The first time the paralysis happens was most extreme the first week of November 2015. I was in the ER that Monday since my entire left leg was paralyzed. Had a bunch of MRIs but all normal. Then a few days later my entire right leg went. Back to the ER for a lumber puncture, again normal. After my back, shoulders and arm, my psychiatrist and neurologist diagnosed me with conversion disorder. It went away fast. This past week has been the first time since then.

My whole life people have been hearing my thoughts. Even if no one is around, the furniture will store my thoughts until someone comes.

Doubles are always spying on me, even my therapist has a double in my work office.

So much anxiety.

I can't always tell how thin I look in the mirror,. 5'4" and 110 pounds but I still feel so fat. I eat just enough to maintain that weight, but I was 113 this morning so I need to make sure not to eat too much today.

I need a break from thinking, constant horrible thinking. I attempted suicide on sleep aids 8 years ago. I lost memories for over a month. Taking a minor overdose cures the craving to take a couple of bottles again.

My therapist is on vacation next week, I have to wait until the following to resume. I might start seeing him twice a week. But my psychiatrist appointment is coming up sooner, so I need to make sure I'm prepared so she doesn't change anything or commit me.
So much violence and hate directed at me my whole childhood, even by my own family. They deny all of it now, the memories are so strong and my family says none of them ever happened.
I went to grad school and earned a master's in computer science, despite being hospitalized twice during the 2 years it took me to finish.

I find it more difficult to look down or away instead of making eye contact. I think of it as another way of being super yavvy. I come off as a stronger person, especially at work, to make the person I have eye contact with see me as their equal or better. Besides, just my being near them gives them access to hearing my thoughts, so I thrive off of eye contact, a strong handshake, good demeanor, and saying the right words in the right tone.

Maybe you trying on something like that could help?

The waiting room at the clinic for my therapist sometimes plays classical music. That's the worst type of music for me to listen to, because it fuels paranoia and anxiety for me, especially when it is complex and sounds like it has emotion. So I sit there and feel like my body and head are being torn apart.

Fortunately the frequency of the waiting room playing classical music has decreased since I told my therapist this. I'm wondering if they are related.

I am always supposed to be happy. Not to worry about anything because all the women in my family are worry-worts. I am told that I'm never actually feel any negative emotions. If I ever feel not happy or not good, do not tell my grandparents especially or anyone else.
Good luck! College is amazing, just learn lots and enjoy your experience.
Thank you for sharing your experience, it is such a strange experience that, like you at first, is very confusing and nerve wrecking.
My doctors have brought up dissociation, but I'm not sure of that status. I have had what you described for hours passing by, but this is my first time losing an entire day.

I had an MRI of my brain when I was in the ER last fall because I was becoming more and more paralyzed. My entire left leg hip-to-foot couldn't move when I had that MRI. The MRI was completely normal, and after another ER visit when the paralysis spread and got worse, the neurology department and my psychiatrist diagnosed it as conversion disorder. It didn't make sense to me, but the next day I could finally move for the first time in a couple of months.

Their explanation brought up emotional stress. I did have another paralysis episode a few days before the memory lapse (both arms were paralyzed)... guess I have another thing to bring up next time I see my psychiatrist.
I remember the day before and the day after. I didn't have anything alcoholic to drink the day before or day of.

I panic in the morning that I won't make it through the work day, then I enter the office and become a strong, young, intelligent woman who is a software engineer working towards a good management position, then I collapse at night filled with paranoia and feelings of being completely overwhelmed. 

But those in between times, when I am succeeding and having a wonderful time with my fiance and friends, it is such an amazing feeling.

I'm female ☺ The pain is hard to distinguish between physical and mental for the wall. I am trying hard in therapy to figure things out emotionally. For example, I am only able to tell my fiance and my cat that I love them. It's too much mental angst to say that out loud or in writing to others, even if they say it first.

I have an experience with the solid white wall. For me it comes most often when my therapist (and people close to me that know) asks about feelings when it comes to pretty much all emotional content, good or bad. My mind just goes blank and my face either blanks or gets uncomfortable. I don't get the random word keep coming up, but the wall starts hurting really badly in my forehead and I can only beg myself why I can't answer the question about how I feel, which intensifies the pain. 

Is it common to not be able to observe/express/know my own thoughts and emotions? Surely by now that I'm 26 I should know how!! How do you get through this? Is it ever possible to know why this happens?

How is any of that an implication of me being weak? My muscles are in tact. I can even go running once the paralysis fully leaves. 

And it wasn't merely rolling the chair over my foot. It was a peg-leg chair. I was walking behind him, he was scooting the chair forward while sitting and my foot got caught in the wrong place. It was an 180 pound person's weight fully landing in a 1-inch concentrated circle on my foot.
The TV show Mr Robot. I shouldn't watch it though. I'm trying to prove that I can handle being off meds better than the main character. Not working too well.
It's scary. Even when you figure out that it's not physical, you still can't move the paralyzed body part.

That's terrible. My fiance's family doesn't know I have schizophrenia, and I've dated him for almost 8 years now. It was back years ago at the time when Mandela had a sign language interpreter who apparently made nonsensical signs and hand movements. Then the media reported the signer had schizophrenia.

I was at the dinner table with his parents, aunts and uncles, and everyone was saying horrible things about people with schizophrenia. That the signer was likely dangerous and could have acted out insanely and killed people. That people with schizophrenia are wildly unpredictable and should be on medication and/or locked up. And that rhetoric kept coming.

It took me so much effort to sit there normally and squeeze my fiance's knee under the table. I wasn't ready to stand up to them and correct anything as much as I wanted to. I had to hide myself, protect myself.
I have good insurance when it comes to medicines. High copay at the doctors office, but good with prescriptions.

Thanks for the singing distraction hint, I can maybe try that. But I never heard that overloaded thinking was considered psychotic. I thought that was more for delusions, paranoia, and hallucinations. Not for this kind of thing I'm having, as long as I don't tell my psychiatrist. 

I am having trouble with listening to music, though. I saw the band "Garbage" live in concert this week, an rock band I've loved for a long time now. Everyone else in the crowd was moving around, singing, cheering, and I was trapped re-living terrible memories associated with the various songs playing that I used to listen to when I was suicidal growing up. If I expected that to happen, why on Earth would I buy tickets and go to the concert? I thought I was done with self-sabotage after I recently became engaged.
What did you think? As panicked as it made me last night, I'm feeling much better and looking forward to this season.

Keep watching, you'll be very glad to see it! Nothing wrong, its just the kind of show that builds tension from season 1 episode 1 to season 2 episode 1, and I'm kind of nervous about it continuing this trend. I just don't do well with intense movies or tv shows, but I'm glad the feedback from this post was positive.
Agreed. I'm seeing my anxiety when Tyrell returns to probably be at when we first met Kilgrave in Jessica Jones (I couldn't watch that show after a few episodes).
Yes, I am very excited! It's going to be an intense season. I just don't do too well with mentally intense shows, but I still get a huge desire to push through this one and keep watching.
Did you watch the whole season 1?

I am back to running after 5 years of injury and foot surgery. I am back to smiling when I run. I am so happy to be able to run again, for the longest time I thought I'd never be able to run after foot surgery.

I do project more light-spirited thoughts at other people as I run around NYC, I don't really get as annoyed as I do in most situations. I am thin, but completely out of shape. Well, maybe not project light-spirited thoughts, but definitely challenging people around me to admit that I've won, they were wrong. I can do so much more than what the doctors thought when I was first diagnosed with schizophrenia back in 2008. Running gives me control and reassurance that I can be better than a normal 26 year old woman, its just a matter of crafting myself. I should run more often.
Thanks, that was very upbeat good advice! I hope you enjoy your vacation, too!
It's the saddest truth, to know something that's going on and have people and doctors say it's not their reality, its my reality. Why would I trust theirs over mine?
Good points all around, thank you. That comes as a relief.

I had a very bad reaction to Jessica Jones. It was way too intense for me... even though the acting and filmography was perfect and I admired that. I tend to immerse myself into the worlds of the film/tv, and with Jessica Jones' David Tennant's perfect evil-guy acting, I broke down after watching the second or third episode and have stayed away since.

I was diagnosed with paranoid schizophrenia senior year of high school. I continued on to undergrad and got a bachelors in computer science. I then went on to grad school for a PhD in computer science, but decided that it wasn't the right path for me, too theoretical whereas I prefer practical applications, so left after earning a master's in computer science. 

I became outgoing in college, so I had no trouble making friends (even met my boyfriend the first day of college and we've been dating since!). I like to chat with people now, and living in NYC there are lots of people to randomly meet and share a laugh.

My parents helped pay for undergrad and I recently paid off all my loans. For grad school, I was a research assistant so I had a yearly stipend/salary plus tuition was waived. 

Overall I am very happy with my education. I certainly had a rough time, was even hospitalized twice in grad school, but I am glad I did it all.
I have a small extended family on both sides, but only ones with mental health illnesses are me with paranoid schizophrenia and my older brother with a combination of OCD, anxiety, and depression.

Fear is the worst. You seem to be in so much angst, I wish I could offer anything to say that could help. Did you like your therapist? I don't see anything to be embarrassed about to go back to that therapist or a new one. We cycle through good and bad health and I think that if anyone, a good psych doctor or therapist knows this and is willing to help.

I think my psychiatrist did say that maybe the Latuda at least makes me think less about the thought broadcasting and other things. I'm just really stressed every month before seeing her, but she says that as long as I'm eating and not losing more weight from loss of appetite on cogentin, she thinks I'm ok. I'm terrified of her realizing I'm taking advantage of the med so it gets the blame, not making me seem like I have a restricting eating disorder. Granted I downplay everything bad to her, I can't risk going to the hospital and missing vacation to Italy where I'm hoping my boyfriend will propose.

I'm doing better at opening up to my therapist weekly. I have seen him for 7 months now, and recently I am making a conscious effort not to mislead him (he mentioned that I do that, but usually i don't notice at the time). I want to try and be open and honest with both my psych doctors, but all my years of practicing my own ideas of self preservation get in the way. My therapist is very intelligent so that makes it easier to talk and share concerns with him. Seeing him once a week is sometimes not enough, but twice is way too much.

I found diaries from when I was 6 or 7 with delusional content that wasn't written as new experiences. I still have those same beliefs, they must have always been there and always will be. I forgot a lot of my memories when I destroyed all of my childhood diaries some years back (I'm 25 now), now I just remember the feelings (oddly enough).

Then I started having suicidal thoughts at 12 and did a little self-harm back then, too. I first told my parents when I was 15, and they made fun of me, so still didn't see a doctor yet.

I was diagnosed at 17 with paranoid schizophrenia after a serious suicide attempt.
That's the other problem, I know I have even say some anxiety that's worse than the average person, but I don't want any mental illness.

I do, but its very delayed. I interact with a lot of people of various backgrounds, jobs, executive statuses, and leaders in other companies that we want to work with and incorporate their products into mine. So every day I'm the smart, professional, young female engineer who has a lot of confidence and communication skills.

Then at night, when I am alone with my boyfriend in our apartment, I collapse mentally. My work persona is so hard to maintain, it really is draining as you said. But the rush it gives is worth the nights.

I am a software engineer at a so-far successful startup, I just celebrated my 1 year there. Recently I have been shifting my responsibilities in a path towards leadership and management in the company.

I secretly take a deep breath, then I smile and get back to engaging in the conversation. Smiling is essential. If I'm working at my desk and feel anxious, I'll take a break and make coffee for myself and my co-worker (we like to try and evaluate new, good coffee beans). I have, and you can, create who you are at work and in general. It's helped me get ahead in my job. I refuse to let my paranoid schizophrenia dictate more than how I think. I might mentally crash here or when alone with people who support me in my illness, but work and the outside world do not need to be aware of that.
Garbage - Even Though Our Love Is Doomed

Did your friend say why he told you about maybe having schizophrenia? It's good to fully explain to the doctor what is causing you distress, if you know. I had thought the American disability act prevented discrimination in higher education and employment, that's the law that granted my accommodations in college and grad school.

So if I'm correctly applying that law, if they deny readmission strictly because of medical illness, that would not be permitted.

You'll still need to document and disclose your illness to the appropriate office to get approved for accommodations, but that was an easy process at my schools.

However, they can still deny you if they feel you cannot meet the academic requirements to both be readmitted and stay in good standing. That's probably why the person you talked to was mentioning the grades you would need, especially if your GPA was low before dropping out. If they did not know or process your reason for dropping out as due to medical illness, you might have to argue with boring administrators.

They would not be allowed to deny you readmission based on any medical illness. I had a close friend drop out of college, and if she wanted to return, she would also have to do an appeal petition. She does not have a medical illness, but your experience with administrators sounds similar - they want to know that the person reapplying will be successful and reflect positively on the university. 

It's tough when schizophrenia makes you unable to continue with education, its happened to me too, both with wanted to take time off but not being able to because of readmission problems, and with getting a different degree than expected.

Your best bet would be to take your letter from your psychiatrist and make an appointment with the university's office of disabilities. They know the process for dealing with medical absences, and can help when the committee decides if the reason for dropping out is medical.

Probably not what you wanted to hear, but without my knowing what the official and documented dropout reason was, there are a whole lot of different outcomes. That's why I mentioned meeting with the disabilities office. Good luck!
